data.why: the repo's examples/ directory already contains minimal_v2.json (a small zika-based v2 dataset) plus v1-format and additional-colours test fixtures; auspice view serves any directory of dataset JSONs directly, so pointing it at examples/ avoids a network fetch for data.nextstrain.org/zika.json

goals: load a time-scaled phylogenetic tree and see how the pathogen lineage diverged over time
colour the tree by a trait (e.g. country, region) or by genotype to spot clusters
filter the dataset by region and date range to focus on a specific outbreak window
cross-reference the tree with the map panel to read likely transmission between locations
inspect the entropy/diversity panel to find variable genomic positions
switch between available example datasets (v2 minimal, v1 minimal) to compare formats

review.summary: The tree captures Auspice's purpose well: reading how a pathogen spread from a dated tree linked to a map. Its phases, tasks and cited screens are accurate; all 11 screens I opened show what their nodes say. It needs a fix before filing because the example data hid the genomic-diversity half of the tool (entropy, genotype colouring) and it leaves out sharing a view, and a few tasks carry dead-end clicks and one missing step.
